# CS 27.45 — General (performance)

> [!summary]
> CS 27.45 fixes the conditions under which small rotorcraft performance is
> determined. It is a CS-27 specification, not a CS-E one, and the rotorcraft
> applicant owns it. Performance is met for still air and a standard atmosphere,
> and it corresponds to the engine power available under the particular ambient
> conditions, flight condition and relative humidity. Available power is engine
> power less installation and accessory losses. A pre-take-off power check is
> required for a turbine engine.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-27's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Unless otherwise prescribed, meet the performance requirements of this Subpart for still air and a standard atmosphere. | Required |
| **(b)** | Make the performance correspond to the engine power available under the particular ambient atmospheric conditions, the particular flight condition, and the relative humidity specified in (d) or (e), as appropriate. | Required |
| **(c)** | Take the available power as engine power, not exceeding the approved power, less the two deductions of (c)(1) and (c)(2). | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Deduct installation losses. | Required |
| **(c)(2)** | Deduct the power absorbed by the accessories and services appropriate to the particular ambient atmospheric conditions and the particular flight condition. | Required |
| **(d)** | For reciprocating engine-powered rotorcraft, base the performance, as affected by engine power, on a relative humidity of 80% in a standard atmosphere. | Required |
| **(e)** | For turbine engine-powered rotorcraft, base the performance, as affected by engine power, on the relative humidity of (e)(1) and (e)(2). | Required |
| **(e)(1)** | The value at and below standard temperature is 80%. | Statement |
| **(e)(2)** | The value at and above standard temperature plus 28°C (50°F) is 34%. | Statement |
| **(e)(2)** | Between these two temperatures, vary the relative humidity linearly. | Required |
| **(f)** | For turbine engine-powered rotorcraft, provide a means to permit the pilot to determine prior to take-off that each engine is capable of developing the power necessary to achieve the applicable rotorcraft performance prescribed in this Subpart. | Required |

CS-27 states the atmosphere in one sentence: "Unless otherwise prescribed, the
performance requirements of this Subpart must be met for still air and a
standard atmosphere" [ext CS 27.45(a)]. There is no sea-level datum and no
approved range of atmospheric variables. [[CS 29.45|CS 29.45(b)]] sets both,
and the difference is substantive.

Sub-point (b) has no CS-29 counterpart. It is the clause that ties the
performance to the real day: the performance "must correspond to the engine
power available under the particular ambient atmospheric conditions, the
particular flight condition, and the relative humidity specified in
sub-paragraphs (d) or (e), as appropriate" [ext CS 27.45(b)]. CS-29 reaches the
same frame from the other end, through its approved range of atmospheric
variables. CS-27 also has no counterpart to CS 29.45(a), which fixes normal
piloting skill and the absence of exceptionally favourable conditions.

Sub-point (c) differs in its second deduction only. CS-27 takes the accessory
and services power "appropriate to the particular ambient atmospheric
conditions and the particular flight condition" [ext CS 27.45(c)(2)]. CS-29
takes it "at the values for which certification is requested and approved"
[ext CS 29.45(c)(2)]. CS-27 varies the set with the condition; CS-29 fixes one
approved set. The opening words of (c) are identical in both codes.

Sub-points (d), (e) and (f) are the same in substance in both codes. Both carry
80% at and below standard temperature and 34% at and above standard temperature
plus 28°C (50°F), and both vary the humidity linearly between those two
temperatures. In the CS-27 text the linear-variation sentence runs on from
(e)(2); in CS-29 it stands as a separate sentence after it. The values and the
rule are the same. Sub-point (f) differs only in the hyphenation of "turbine
engine-powered" and in the capitalisation of Subpart.

## Bearing on this engine

CS 27.45 creates no CS-E obligation. It binds the rotorcraft applicant, who
determines the performance of the installed aircraft. What the point does is
consume engine data, and CS-E names that data in three places.

**Approved power.** Sub-point (c) caps the available power at engine power "not
exceeding the approved power" [ext CS 27.45(c)]. Those are the ratings
established under [[CS-E 40]] and listed in the type certificate data sheet
[CS-E 40(e)]. This engine declares Take-off Power and Maximum Continuous Power
[CS-E 40(a)], Rated 30-Minute Power [CS-E 40(b)(4)] and three OEI ratings
[CS-E 40(b)(3)].

**The basis of the declared power.** CS-E declares the ratings on standard
atmospheric conditions, with no air bleed for aircraft services and with only
the accessories essential for engine functioning installed [CS-E 40(c)]. Any
other basis is declared in the type certificate data sheet [CS-E 40(c)].
Sub-point (c) of CS 27.45 starts from that figure and subtracts installation
losses [ext CS 27.45(c)(1)] and accessory and services power
[ext CS 27.45(c)(2)]. The engine-level half of that subtraction reaches the
installer as the installation losses definable at engine level of
[[AMC E 20|AMC E 20(f)(1)]].

**Ambient conditions and humidity.** CS-27 asks more of the engine data here
than CS-29 does, because its sub-points (b) and (c)(2) both work at the
particular ambient atmospheric conditions and the particular flight condition
[ext CS 27.45(b)], [ext CS 27.45(c)(2)]. The engine-side supply is
[[CS-E 20|CS-E 20(e)]]: the engine performance data must include means of
determining the effect on performance of engine bleed, power off-take, forward
speed, ambient pressure, temperature and humidity [CS-E 20(e)]. The conditions
the engine is approved for are an assumption about the installation. They are
submitted before engine certification and carried in the instructions for
installation under [[CS-E 30|CS-E 30(a)]], and the operating limitations for the
intended operating conditions are established under [CS-E 40(d)].

**Power assurance.** Sub-point (f) is the pre-take-off power check, and it is
the same obligation in both codes. CS-E answers it directly: for an engine
having one or more OEI ratings, the applicant provides data on engine
performance characteristics and variability so that the aircraft manufacturer
can establish power assurance procedures [CS-E 20(f)]. The scope of that data is
set by [[AMC E 20|AMC E 20(f)(1)]], which names this sub-point as one of the two
specifications the data serves [AMC E 20(f)(1)]. This engine declares three OEI
ratings, so [[CS-E 20|CS-E 20(f)]] binds.

Which engine parameters that means reads is open in both codes. Provision for
engine instrumentation is a separate CS-E obligation [[CS-E 60|CS-E 60(a)]], and
the item is recorded in [[CS 29.45]].

**What does not reach this engine.** Sub-point (d) is for reciprocating
engine-powered rotorcraft and has no bearing on a turboshaft [ext CS 27.45(d)].

[VERIFY: whether the installation is certificated under CS-27 or CS-29. The
counterpart point [[CS 29.45]] sets the atmospheric frame differently and
qualifies the accessory deduction differently. An engine offered for both codes
supplies the data both readings need. [[CS-E 30]] carries the same open item.]
